CO binding causes a displacement of the C- helix, and that binding of DNA causes a further displacement of C- helix.

UV and visible resonance raman spectroscopy has revealed the local displacement of the C-terminal helix of CooA by CO binding, and further displacement by DNA binding, which is the first experimental evidence for this mechanism of signal transduction.

UV and visible resonance raman spectroscopy revealed the structural changes in the C-helmix and heme of CO-sensing transcriptional regulator CooA from the bacteria Rhodospirilium rubrum upon binding of CO and DNA, which is the ligand and the target of CooA, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of the CO sensor and transcriptional regulator CooA.
the mechanism of the CO sensor in CooA.
the structural changes in the C-helm of the DNA-binding domain of the CO sensor CooA upon CO binding, and the effect of DNA binding on the CO binding site of CooA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CO binding to CooA causes a displacement of the C- helix, and that DNA binding to the CO-bound form causes further displacement of the helix in the same direction.

the CO binding and DNA binding to CooA induce the same type of displacement of the C- helix, but in opposite directions, and that this movement is a common structural element in the activation process.

CO binding to the sensor domain of CooA induces movement of the DNA-binding domain, and binding of DNA to the DNA-binding domain induces further movement in the same direction, leading to the complete active state.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the C-helmix displacement is a common feature for the CO binding and DNA binding of CooA.
the CO binding to the CooA heme causes the displacement of the C-terminal helix, which is the hinge region between the sensor and DNA-binding domain.
the C-helical movement is a key element in the activation mechanism of CooA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the heme and the C-helix are displaced by a distance of 3.3 A in the DNA-bound active form.
the DNA-binding domain of CooA undergoes a large conformational change upon CO binding.
the C-helical displacement is an important factor in the CO sensor mechanism of CooA.
